ruling.reasoning:
The case is filed as a safety incident: the rider complains that the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked for my number. I felt harassed and unsafe" [F1]. The trace marks the SAFE-1 element as pass — a safety complaint exists and no automatic ruling is permitted; the allowed outcome is escalate, and SAFE-1 requires the judge to stop and hand the matter to a human with a factual summary [SAFE-1]. The complaint as worded describes unwanted sexual advances / harassment aimed at the rider by the driver, which is exactly the conduct SAFE-1 and Ryde's code of conduct bar without tolerating it.

The record does not settle the substance either way: there is no in-app chat at all [F3], and the only contrary account is the driver's own post-trip statement, "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened," which is a statement, not a system record, and cannot outweigh the rider's account on a safety question [F4]. There is nothing in the GPS or fare records bearing on the alleged remarks: the trip is essentially on-route (17.1 km actual vs 17.2 km optimal, -0.1 km [F1]) and only 2.2 minutes over estimate [F2], so no route or fare clause is engaged.

What a human reviewer should check: the driving records already in hand [F1][F2]; the rider's complaint as filed on the safety incident [F1]; the absence of any in-app chat and the fact that the driver's denial was written only after the trip [F3][F4]; and the parties' histories, noting there are no prior disputes or upheld incidents for either party [F5][F6]. Both profiles are background only and cannot decide anything here. Because the trace fixes the safety branch and bars an automatic ruling, the amount is left unset and the outcome is escalate.
